disagreements.topic: Exit multiple: 23x (agent_1) vs 24x (agents 2-5), and whether the rate move gets counted twice

Some compression as the forward year rolls is normal, so 24x is the better central exit multiple and 23x is a bear-leaning choice. Reconciled fair value is $535.

thesis_break_reason: $365 is just above the 2026-09-15 intraday low ($362.55) and about 19x the FY27 non-GAAP EPS guide. A close there gives back the whole Investor Day re-rating and would most likely mean the guide is no longer believed: a Design IP miss or FY27 cut at the December print, renewed China EDA curbs (~10% of revenue), or a credible AI/open-source share-loss story. Rates alone more plausibly take the stock to ~$400-420 (21-22x), not $365.
key_drivers: FY27 guide (Investor Day release): revenue $11.10-11.20B (+15%), non-GAAP EPS $19.04-19.12, FCF ~$3.1B, SBC ~$970M, mid-20s EPS CAGR FY26-30, ~$1B buyback; the December Q4 FY26 print is the first test

Balance sheet: net debt ~$6.4B, all floating-rate term loans repaid in Q1 FY26, so the hike hits the multiple, not EPS; ~$1.02B principal due in each of FY27 and FY28

Blend ~$535 as of Oct 2027 using 10-Q net debt of $6.4B. That is slightly above the round-2 mean ($532) because agent_1's 23x partly double-counts a rate move already in today's multiple.

summary: Round 2 converged: the five forecasters now put P(close >= $491 on 2027-10-01) at 0.515-0.60, with a mean of 0.556 and fair values of $519-540. My checks confirmed the facts that matter (10-year at 4.99%, floating-rate term loans repaid so the hike hits the multiple rather than EPS, TSMC on Oct 15) and corrected only minor ones (the Kimi drop was -7.85%; HSBC's $700 predates Investor Day), so I keep the mean ladder. Reconciled fair value is $535, about 9% above spot, with a fat left tail (45% realized vol, China, IP credibility, AI-disruption scares). The thesis breaks below $365. The expected return is roughly SPY-like at about three times the volatility, so there is no checked risk-adjusted edge.
